brief.headline: Nifty Set for Cues from Global AI Surge; Defence, Auto and AC Stocks in Focus
brief.summary: Indian equities enter Thursday after Nifty climbed 1.14% to 25514.3 and Bank Nifty surged 1.65% to 63063.0, aided by strong auto performance and softer crude at 90.16. Global risk appetite is buoyed by Anthropic's record-breaking public debut, which lifted US tech futures. Key domestic triggers include proposed defence capex hikes, cooling copper prices benefiting cooling appliance makers, and regulatory updates across telecom and payments.

takeaways.text: Anthropic's record IPO pricing at $83 per share sparked global risk-on sentiment, driving Nasdaq futures up 2.04% and lifting technology sentiment.
Defence stocks HAL, BEL and BDL rallied up to 3% as the Ministry of Defence seeks a 20% capex increase for FY28.
Copper prices dropping to seven-month lows triggered gains of up to 6% in AC makers Voltas, Blue Star, and PG Electroplast.
JPMorgan maintained an Overweight rating on Reliance Industries with a target of ₹1,675, citing 23% upside driven by O2C earnings.
Paytm and Pine Labs fell up to 7% on reports that UPI MDR implementation may be delayed until H1CY27 after state elections.
Tata Tech jumped over 9% after announcing an FY30 revenue target of $1.1-1.3 billion versus approximately $620 million in FY26.

sections.india: Domestic equities saw broad gains yesterday led by Nifty Auto climbing to 28,111.95, with Maruti, Hero Moto, and Eicher rallying up to 7.58%. Cooling raw material prices supported consumer durables, as copper hitting seven-month lows lifted AC makers like Voltas and Blue Star up to 6%. Meanwhile, proposed 20% capex growth by the Defence Ministry sparked up to 3% gains across BEL, BDL, and HAL. In financial technology, payment providers faced pressure following reports that UPI MDR could be delayed until H1CY27.
sections.world: Wall Street futures advanced sharply overnight, with Nasdaq futures rising 2.04% and S&P 500 futures gaining 1.20% ahead of Anthropic's trading debut. In commodities, Brent crude slipped 1.95% to 90.16, while gold traded near 3717.8 after touching a 14-month low. The US 10Y yield dropped 3.7 bps to 5.07, even as Fed October minutes confirmed a planned December hike and highlighted inflation risks from AI infrastructure build-outs. Geopolitics drew attention as Donald Trump met Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
sections.tech: Anthropic achieved a historic market debut, pricing its offering at $83 per share to raise $81 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation, with total proceeds reaching $107.3 billion including private placements. The blockbuster listing revitalised global AI sentiment, although commentators noted emerging competitive friction and governance changes at Nvidia following Jensen Huang's exit. In Indian startups, physical AI venture Humyn Labs secured $47 million in Series A funding to expand global testing facilities. Additionally, Alibaba reported a 10% revenue increase backed by substantial AI hardware spending in China.
